Note::contains_any_alpha¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::contains_any_alpha() const

Test Whether A Cell Has At Least One Letter¶

contains_any_alpha() reports, for each cell, whether any byte is an ASCII letter (A–Z, a–z). It is the “some” counterpart of is_alpha’s “all”: use it to separate rows that carry text from rows that are pure numbers, codes, or punctuation.

The check is ASCII-only — a cell whose only letters are non-ASCII (é, 日) returns 0 unless it also has an ASCII letter. An empty cell returns 0.

Return value¶

A Bool Note with the receiver’s shape, one native truth value per cell. Use bools() for a borrowed contiguous host view.

Example 1: A Batch¶

const auto n = pluss::make_note({"abc", "abc123", "123", "-42-", "", "a1"});
const auto mask = n.contains_any_alpha();
std::cout << "[";
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < mask.bools().size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << static_cast<int>(mask.bools()[i]);
std::cout << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1]
